en: Puggalapaññatti Mātikā 2.
Enumeration of Pairs (Dukauddesa)
Two types of persons:
one who is prone to anger and one who harbors resentment;
one who is contemptuous and one who is spiteful.
Envious and stingy;
fraudulent and deceitful;
shameless and reckless.
He is difficult to speak with and has evil friends.
He guards the doors of his sense faculties poorly and lacks moderation in eating.
He is muddle-minded and lacks clear comprehension.
One who has failed in virtue and one who has failed in view;
one who is fettered internally and one who is fettered externally;
one who is without anger and one who is without malice.
Free from hypocrisy and free from disparagement;
free from envy and free from avarice;
free from deceit and free from guile.
Modest and scrupulous;
easy to speak to and possessed of good friends;
guarding the doors of the sense faculties and moderate in eating.
One who is established in mindfulness and clearly comprehending;
one who is perfected in virtue and perfected in view.
These two persons are rare in the world.
Two persons are difficult to satisfy;
two persons are easy to satisfy.
For two persons, the taints increase.
The taints do not increase for two kinds of persons:
one who is intent on the inferior and one who is intent on the sublime;
one who is satisfied and one who satisfies others.
The Dyads.
